paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. David says the fool says in his heart, "There is no God." (Psalm 53:1) That's a quiet sentence, and it can start in a quiet place. Nobody has to say it out loud for it to steer a whole life.

But look UP, because God doesn't look away. God looks down from heaven "to see if any understand, if any seek God." (Psalm 53:2) Then the song says, "All have turned away, they have together become corrupt; there is no one who does good, not even one." (Psalm 53:3) I think that's the honest part nobody wants to read twice, and it includes me and it includes you. That's why I keep asking myself who I'm actually listening to when it gets quiet in my own heart.

So where does the song land? It doesn't land on despair. David ends with a longing: "Oh, that the salvation of Israel would come from Zion!" (Psalm 53:6) He looks past the mess and asks for God to rescue, and when God restores His captive people, he says, "let Jacob rejoice, let Israel be glad!" (Psalm 53:6) So take the honest look, friend, and then take the gladness, because our hope was never in us.
